boundary_calibration.assessment: Boundary calibration is the strongest coverage dimension. Most habits are soft defaults, and many probes require deciding when price, schedule, route simplicity, rating source, location, or service details limit the habit.

drift_handling.assessment: Not covered. The verified revision count is zero, and no probe requires replacing an older stable policy with later durable evidence.

exception_retention.assessment: Exception retention is thin. Only the breakfast/location probes meaningfully require treating paid-breakfast choices as conditional exceptions rather than durable revision. Most other apparent exceptions are just ordinary soft-boundary cases.

false_personalization.assessment: Not covered as a primary construct. Several items prevent overgeneralization of an existing habit, but none requires concluding that evidence is insufficient or conflicting and therefore refusing to personalize.

habit_induction.assessment: Habit induction is broadly present because every item assumes a latent user default. It is primary mainly when the correct answer is direct use of the learned default rather than a boundary or exception decision.

overall_gaps: No drift_handling is present: verified_revision_version_count is 0 and no probe requires durable policy replacement.
No true false_personalization probe is present: none asks the assistant to withhold personalization because evidence is insufficient or conflicting.
Exception_retention is underrepresented; most probes that look like exceptions are better classified as ordinary soft boundary calibration.

Several items contain choice-letter or rationale mismatches that threaten annotation clarity: tm_pd_v04_user_000_h02_p01, tm_pd_v04_user_000_h02_p02, tm_pd_v04_user_000_h02_p03, tm_pd_v04_user_000_h03_p00, tm_pd_v04_user_000_h03_p01, tm_pd_v04_user_000_h03_p02, tm_pd_v04_user_000_h03_p04, tm_pd_v04_user_000_h04_p01, and tm_pd_v04_user_000_h05_p06.

Many gold choices are also attractive under generic travel reasoning such as nonstop routing, shorter walks, better ratings, or lower friction. Tighter matched pairs are needed to isolate the latent habit as the causal variable.
The provided capability taxonomy lacks an explicit cross-context-transfer category, so those intended probes collapse into habit_induction or boundary_calibration in this audit.

pair_opportunities.gap: A natural default-versus-boundary pair exists, but a tighter matched pair should vary only carrier/value while holding timing, stops, and fare nearly constant.
pair_opportunities.reason: The same soft Delta habit yields a Delta recommendation when comparable and non-Delta or mixed recommendations when Delta worsens schedule, routing, or price.

pair_opportunities.gap: The matched opportunity is present, but several rationales have choice-letter errors and should be corrected before use as clean evidence.
pair_opportunities.reason: The afternoon-return habit produces afternoon returns in default scope, but near-midday or otherwise cleaner returns when the literal afternoon option is unattractive; it also must not be applied to outbound legs.

pair_opportunities.gap: Missing a true exception pair where an explicit price cap, schedule emergency, or user instruction makes a long layover or second connection correct. The Boise audit item has a cap, but all options are under it, so it still tests the default.
pair_opportunities.reason: Current probes mostly show the default preference for one comfortable layover and the boundary against long waits, tight changes, or multiple connections.

pair_opportunities.gap: Missing a matched exception where Maya explicitly sets a lower rating floor, asks for cheapest regardless of quality, or has only sub-4.0 suitable options.
pair_opportunities.reason: Existing items use and calibrate the customer-rating floor across family/work contexts and rating scales, but they almost always still select a qualifying public score.

pair_opportunities.gap: A usable default-versus-boundary pair exists, but exception-retention coverage would be cleaner with one explicit historical paid-breakfast exception and a later matched default case.
pair_opportunities.reason: The breakfast habit chooses included breakfast when location and logistics remain close, but gives way to materially better no-car location or refuses to upgrade merely for a hotter breakfast.

probe_audits.reason: The Delta preference is explicitly soft. The item requires applying the carrier habit only within comparable schedule/stop/value bounds and choosing American when Delta is materially worse.
The correct choice uses a non-Delta nonstop because the Delta nonstop is meaningfully more expensive and the cheaper Delta option has a connection. This is a value boundary on a soft preference.
The mixed ticket applies the Delta default where it works on the outbound, but overrides it on the return because the all-Delta return is too tight. This is leg-level boundary calibration, not drift.

The item mainly tests use of the induced soft Delta carrier default in a new but still in-scope ATL-origin trip. It also calibrates the preference by choosing the more comfortable Delta connection rather than any Delta option blindly.
The probe distinguishes a return-leg afternoon preference from an unsupported outbound timing rule. Choosing the morning outbound with an afternoon nonstop return measures scope calibration.

Under the actual choices, the gold noon nonstop is a clean near-afternoon boundary case that beats a literal midafternoon return with a tight connection and late arrival. The supplied rationale appears to swap option labels, but the mechanism is still boundary calibration.

The item uses the induced afternoon-return default to choose the nonstop 3:15 p.m. return despite a higher fare. The gold rationale contains an A/C label error, but the semantic decision is the default return-timing habit under close fares.

The probe requires not overgeneralizing the habit to Wednesday outbound timing and instead applying it to the Friday return. The rationale text appears to name the wrong option, but the actual gold choice has the nonstop afternoon return.
The afternoon-return default is softened when the remaining true afternoon choice adds a connection. A near-midday nonstop after breakfast is the calibrated boundary response.

The item uses the induced preference for at most one short layover, choosing the manageable 75-minute connections over cheaper long waits, extra stops, or extreme departure timing. The provided rationale mislabels the winning option.

For a personal family trip where all options connect, the gold choice reflects the learned one-comfortable-layover pattern. The rationale text refers to the wrong choice letter, but the choice content supports the mechanism.

The Quebec City item transfers the induced layover preference to a simple international itinerary: one manageable connection each way beats multiple connections, long waits, or tight changes. The supplied rationale again names the wrong option.

The item tests not overreading the habit as a desire for stopovers or long layovers. It calibrates the preference toward one comfortable connection and away from long waits, extra stops, or tight transfers.

Although labeled as an exception, all fares are under the cap, so the price-cap exception is not active. The probe instead tests keeping the default simple one-connection hold rather than minimizing fare with extra stops, long waits, or tight changes; the label rationale has option-name confusion.

The family-hotel decision uses the induced customer-review floor, preferring a practical 4.1-rated hotel over a cheaper/larger 3.8-rated option. It also treats the rating as one screen among location and room-fit constraints.

The item calibrates the construct as public guest rating rather than official hotel-class stars. The label rationale names a different option than the gold, but the gold choice reflects the 4-plus public-score habit without demanding luxury.

The work-hotel choice depends on the induced 4.0-ish public rating floor, not just lowest price or shuttle convenience. It also avoids turning the floor into a requirement to pick the highest-rated or fanciest property.

The item tests that the rating habit is a floor, not a mandate to chase the highest rating. The 4.1 hotel wins because it clears the floor while fitting the no-car, rate, room, breakfast, and location tradeoffs.
The probe calibrates the habit around known customer-facing ratings: a missing public score should not be assumed acceptable, while a far airport hotel should not win merely because it is 4.5-rated.
The item tests scale calibration by mapping the 4-out-of-5 style guest-rating floor to an approximately 8-out-of-10 verified-score site. It is not a Google-only or official-star-class rule.

The Seattle work stay uses the induced included-breakfast preference as a tie-breaker when commute, rating, and cap compliance remain close. It does not let breakfast override a materially worse location.

The breakfast preference is soft and gives way to a materially better no-car family base. The item also preserves the idea that paid-breakfast choices are conditional exceptions, not a permanent abandonment of the breakfast preference.

The family school-weekend decision applies the induced included-breakfast preference because the breakfast-included hotel is also walkable for the morning program. The habit is used only because the location remains competitive.
For early work sessions, the induced breakfast preference breaks a close tie between otherwise walkable, refundable, under-cap hotels. This is default use of a soft service preference.

The robotics-tournament item applies the induced breakfast preference in a busy family-morning context while preserving venue walkability. It is not just a generic cheapest or highest-rated hotel selection.

The item calibrates breakfast as an included-service preference, not a hot-buffet or premium-breakfast requirement. Keeping the current quiet, close, breakfast-included hold is the calibrated response.

The rationale explicitly treats prior paid-breakfast choices as trip-specific compromises rather than a durable revision. The current comparable breakfast-included option should win; the label rationale appears to name A even though the actual breakfast-included primary is C.
